newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish stock market booms on investment trusts.
newsitem.headline: Spanish stock market booms on investment trusts.

text.p: The Madrid stock market has been hitting a string of record highs on the back of a sharp increase in net inflows from investment trusts and this bull run is seen continuing, analysts said on Thursday.
Key money rates are at historic lows, luring savings from traditional deposit accounts and swelling investment trusts, which have focused on shares as a high-yielding option.
As a result, since the end of March the blue chip Ibex-35 index has risen 18 percent. On Thursday, the Index hit a new record of 6,495.72 before subsiding to a flat 6,444.88 in late afternoon trade.

According to data from the stock exchange commission CNMV, in the year to March FIM unit trusts --which buy bonds and stocks-- doubled assets to 11.6 trillion pesetas from 5.7 trillion one year before.
This adds to investment firms' unit trusts (SIM), which stood at 12.07 trillion pesetas at the end of March 1997.
At the end of March, Spanish FIMs had 7.46 percent invested in shares, with 40.1 percent concentrated in government debt and another 36.4 percent in the money market.
Managed savings invested in equities increased by around 300 billion pesetas in March versus December, the CNMV said.
Juan Cueto, an analyst at Ibersecurities brokerage, said investment funds were growing faster than anticipated.

"We had an initial forecast of new collective investment in equities of 800 billion pesetas for the full year. If the first quarter rate is mantained, the end of 1997 will see a total of more than one trillion pesetas," he said.
Low bond yields are attracting money toward shares.
"Money inflows to the stock market will continue," said Angel Garcia Menendez, economist at Inverbolsa.
"One-year or 18-month bill yields stand at around five percent, while stocks have gained 25 percent in less than five months, and still have scope to rise more," he added.
Besides the big jump in investment trusts, there were other factors supporting stocks, such as individual retail buying or institutional investors buying direct stakes in big firms, analysts said.
Moreover the rally which has brought both indices and volumes to record highs, shows no signs of letting up.
In the first four months of the year, traded volume at the Madrid stock exchange rose to 6.35 trillion pesetas versus 3.64 trillion pesetas in the year-ago same period.
Another one trillion pesetas' worth of trading volume may be added in May alone, analysts said.
"Stocks are the buy of the year. So in recent months we've moved money there," a trader at one of the biggest Spanish banks said.
"April and May (alone) could be even better than the first quarter," said Ibersecurities' Cueto.
According to the Spanish association of investment and pension funds (Inverco), total FIM unit trusts rose by 250 billion pesetas in April. A good part of this rise was due to higher market prices.
But the rise also reflects the improvement in yield on these unit trusts.
The average yield of equities FIMs during the first four months was 12.03 percent. The same value for bonds-equities FIMs was 3.5 percent, while for bonds alone the trusts earned 1.67 percent.
